text: CPI has surged to 4.2% (a 3-year high) and the Fed is now signaling a possible rate hike by late 2026 — this is a meaningful shift from easing to potential tightening that could pressure growth stocks and valuations across your portfolio.
Sell RGTI — it's down 35%, over 60% off its high, revenue is shrinking by 34%, it's unprofitable with nearly 19% short interest, and there's no credible recovery catalyst in sight.

Sell SGLP.L — this commodity holding is down 17.5% with rock-bottom relative strength at -99, meaning it's weaker than virtually everything else in the market, and the technical picture offers no reason to hold.
Sell RDW — Redwire has negative earnings, negative cash flow, 22% short interest, and the EXIT signal confirms the thesis is broken with no fundamental support to justify staying in.

Trim IONQ — despite flashy 202% revenue growth, it's deeply unprofitable, burning cash, carries 16% short interest, and in a rising-rate environment unprofitable speculative names face the most valuation pressure.
Trim QBTS — this quantum computing stock is down 19% with negative earnings, negative free cash flow, and nearly 19% short interest, so reduce your exposure before further deterioration.

Add to ADBE — a PE of just 7 with 10.5% revenue growth and strong cash flow makes Adobe look significantly undervalued, and it's the kind of profitable, cash-generating business that holds up well if rates stay higher.

Add to META — a PE of 16 paired with 22% revenue growth and solid free cash flow is a genuinely rare combination for a company this size, making it one of the better risk-reward setups in your portfolio.
